output.summary: Soft-wooded shrub native to eastern Australia; in New Zealand it is reported as indigenous, though some authorities consider it introduced. It has blue-purple flowers and orange-red to scarlet fruit. Ripe berries were traditional Māori food and were stewed or made into pies and jam by early European settlers; using leaves in hāngī is now discouraged because they contain poisonous alkaloids.
